sections.title: Serial dependence and the regression problem
sections.summary: High fit combined with strongly autocorrelated residuals motivates reexamining conventional econometric inference. ARIMA representations, differencing, and near-random-walk behavior explain why many economic levels contain strong persistence.

sections.title: Why independent series can appear related

source_span.start_text: Let us consider the usual linear regression model

sections.summary: Standard regression significance tests rely on an error structure that fails when unrelated dependent and explanatory series are highly autocorrelated. Sampling variability in correlations can therefore produce high fit without a genuine relationship.

sections.title: Simulation evidence on spurious significance

sections.summary: Simulations of independent random walks and integrated moving-average series produce frequent false significance and high fit, increasingly so with more irrelevant regressors. Differencing sharply improves results, though residual moving-average dependence can still distort tests.

sections.title: Diagnostics and defensible time-series modeling

source_span.start_text: It has been well known for some time now
source_span.end_text: the warnings given in the text books about this possibility.

sections.summary: Strong residual autocorrelation signals misspecification regardless of fit, and simple corrections are not guaranteed cures. The authors recommend examining time-series structure, comparing levels with changes, and judging theoretical models by whether their residuals retain explainable information.
